blueprint_inputs.why: Fixture-by-fixture Monte Carlo is the structural engine that maps strengths to season outcomes.
Strength posterior and drift determine tail probabilities and avoid over-sharp futures.
Order, venues and rival fixtures shift expected points among equal-rated teams.
Tiebreak order and slot allocation decide close cut-offs.
Sanctions shift points irrespective of on-pitch strength.
Depth affects strength under injuries and congestion over the horizon.
Current long-term absences adjust remaining-season strength.
Window moves and manager changes update stale ratings.
Early-season futures lean on priors until matches accumulate.
Multi-competition load links separate futures for the same team.
Leverage tells which remaining fixtures matter for the cut-off.
Sharp futures and match prices are strong priors for ratings.
Contract wording defines the exact qualifying outcome (including playoff/ET handling).
Top-N rungs must be consistent with winner and relegation probabilities.
xG-based ratings are less noisy than points for long-horizon strength.
Elo/Dixon-Coles ratings are the strength input to the simulation.
Late-season incentives change effort and rotation in simulated fixtures.
Postponed/abandoned fixtures reshuffle the schedule and can void markets.
Knockout advancement beyond 90 minutes includes shootouts.
Advancement-wording markets include extra time and penalties.
Aggregate state in two-legged ties.

unreg:fifa_ranking_outcome.blueprint_mechanism: Season-outcome futures (title, top-N, relegation, qualification, advancement, outright, host, trophies) are the outcome of a stochastic tournament: remaining fixtures are simulated from team strengths with uncertainty and drift, then tiebreak and slot rules are applied. The mechanism is the aggregate of many match outcomes, so value comes from correct rating uncertainty, schedule strength, rule details, squad depth and injuries, and correlation across teams. Long-horizon prices embed more information drift than match prices, so the underlying rating prior and rule parsing matter most.
unreg:fifa_ranking_outcome.label: FIFA ranking outcomes

live_series.reviewer_reason: FIFA ranking top-10 outcome tied to the World Cup; no market listed so unverified. A formula-based governing-body ranking decided by match results and weights.
live_series.title: World Cup FIFA Top 10

unreg:fifa_ranking_outcome.target: A national team's rank or presence in the top 10 of the FIFA men's world ranking at a stated date.
unreg:fifa_ranking_outcome.why_distinct: Resolved by FIFA's points formula and match weighting after results, a governing-body ranking calculation unlike a standings finish or a voted award.

blueprint_inputs.why: Full distribution (variance, skew) of points for threshold and margin markets.
Remaining opponents and venues set expected additional points.
Posterior strength uncertainty widens the distribution of totals.
Current tally, minutes and remaining fixtures set player race outcomes.
Player shot volume and shot quality produce expected remaining goals/assists.
Expected minutes are the largest uncertainty for player counting stats.
Penalty duty adds high-xG chances for scoring totals.
Observed over-performance should be shrunk toward xG-implied production.
Injury hazard truncates player and team output.
Draw variance drives dispersion of points totals.
Defines what is counted (league only, own goals, tie-break rules).
Threshold ladder must be consistent with distribution.
Team-level xG is the strength basis for expected points.
Dead-rubber effects on late-season points.
Shot volume supports player-level rate estimation.
Set-piece role contributes to scoring totals.

unreg:tournament_aggregate_event_props.blueprint_mechanism: Season-stat markets (team points, points margin, player total, season leader) settle on an accumulated count over remaining fixtures. The mechanism is a sum of match-level processes (points or goals) with strength uncertainty, rotation and injury risk, and tie-break or rounding rules. Player stats additionally depend on minutes, role, penalty duty and finishing luck regression; team points depend on schedule strength and draw variance.

unreg:tournament_aggregate_event_props.target: A count, sum or extreme of goals or match events aggregated across many matches in a tournament, relative to a strike or condition.
unreg:tournament_aggregate_event_props.why_distinct: Outcome is an aggregate over a whole tournament (goal environment, shootout frequency, comebacks), not one match total, a player stat or the winner; no existing archetype aggregates many matches.
